description: The figure presents two pie charts comparing error analysis for two models — the Vanilla model (left) and the HCL model (right) — based on the paper “Laying the Foundation First: Investigating the Generalization from Atomic Skills to Complex Reasoning Tasks.” Each chart is divided into four categories, color-coded and labeled in the legend: “Atomic Skill Fail” (dark teal), “Correct” (medium teal), “Reason Error” (light teal), and “Question Misunderstood” (white). In the Vanilla model chart, “Atomic Skill Fail” dominates at 68.0%, followed by “Correct” at 12.0%, “Reason Error” at 12.0%, and “Question Misunderstood” at 8.0%. In contrast, the HCL model chart shows “Correct” as the largest segment at 55.0%, followed by “Reason Error” at 21.0%, “Question Misunderstood” at 14.0%, and “Atomic Skill Fail” at 10.0%. The visual comparison suggests that the HCL model significantly reduces atomic skill failures and increases correct responses compared to the Vanilla model, while exhibiting higher rates of reasoning errors and question misunderstandings. All percentage values are explicitly labeled within each slice, and the charts are presented side-by-side for direct comparison.
